faq: Will the descriptions sound like a robot wrote them?
We start from your best existing copy and tone notes, then a person reads each batch. We avoid filler phrases and repeated openings so product pages read naturally and differently.
How do you avoid wrong claims about my products?
Drafts use only the specs and facts you supply. We do not invent materials, sizes or benefits, and we flag anything unclear for you to confirm instead of guessing.
Which store platforms can you load into?
Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Wix and Squarespace through their import tools or admin. For other platforms, we deliver a clean CSV you can upload.
Can you write in other languages?
Yes in the main European languages, though a native check is wise for key pages. For full page translation with your style kept, see our translations service.
desc:
AI product descriptions for online stores turn titles, specs and photos into clear product copy in your own brand tone. Ecom Swift LLC drafts the text, you approve a first batch, and the final copy is loaded into your store with search titles included.

## What are AI product descriptions for online stores?

They are product page texts drafted from the facts you already hold: the title, the specifications, the variants and the photos. The draft follows a tone and a layout agreed with you, and a person checks it against your specs before it goes live.

The aim is not to replace your voice. It is to produce a consistent first version of hundreds of pages in the time it would take to write a few, so your team can spend its effort on review and on the products that need extra care.

## Why copied supplier text holds a store back

Many catalogs carry the supplier's wording word for word. The same paragraph appears on many competing stores, so search engines have little reason to rank yours above the others, and shoppers see nothing that sounds like your brand.

Thin copy hurts as well. A page that lists only a title and a size chart leaves shoppers to guess about materials, fit and use, and a shopper who guesses often leaves. Original, accurate descriptions answer questions on the page, support a distinct search title and give you copy that matches the way the rest of the store speaks.

## What strong product copy includes

- A short opening line that says what the product is and who it suits.
- Bullet features that start with the benefit and then give the detail.
- Specifications taken from your own data, such as size, material and care.
- Variants and sizes explained, so shoppers know what differs between options.
- A tone that matches your best existing pages, not a generic sales voice.
- A search title and meta description written for each product.
- Honest wording with no claims your specs cannot support.
- Plain sentences that read well on a phone.
- Collection page introductions that frame the group of products.
- A brand style sheet that records tone, words to use and words to avoid.

## How we work

We read three sample pages you like and your best existing descriptions, then agree a tone and a simple layout. Before writing at scale, we draft a small first batch and send it for review. You tell us what sounds right and what does not, and we adjust the rest to match.

Each draft is built from your product data. Where the data is silent, we do not fill the gap with a claim. We flag it for you instead. In the larger packages we check the copy against your specifications for facts such as dimensions, materials and compatibility.

The Basic package delivers a first batch as a sheet or CSV. The Standard package adds search titles and meta descriptions, describes variants, loads the approved text into your store and includes one round of tone changes. The Premium package covers a full catalog pass, writes collection page introductions, produces the brand style sheet and tests the result in your store. Loading works with the main store platforms through import files or direct edits.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Supply accurate specs, because the copy is only as good as the data.
- Read the first batch closely and mark what feels off.
- Keep one tone across the whole catalog.
- Put the most important detail in the first sentence.
- Update the copy when a product changes.

**Avoid:**
- Publishing copy that nobody on your side has read.
- Making health, safety or performance claims without proof.
- Repeating the same opening sentence on every page.
- Stuffing the text with search phrases.
- Copying a competitor's wording, which creates its own problems.

## Who this is for

It suits a store owner with a supplier catalog and hundreds of products that still carry manufacturer text. It suits a brand launching a new range that needs consistent pages before launch day. It also suits a small team that writes well but cannot keep up with the volume of new products.

## What we need from you

Send a product export, your brand notes and three examples of pages you consider well written. Tell us about words you prefer or want avoided, and the languages you sell in. We never need your password: if we load the text into your store, access is given as a collaborator, staff or developer user with limited permissions, and you can review everything before it goes live.
